purpose: Run one training group and one synthetic sealed-evaluation group through every authority this sprint added, before any bulk campaign spends a container, and close the two items W2 and W3b deferred.

steps.name: rights-clean package and four opaque candidates
pre-outcome features stored before verifier results
role-bound projection from the sealed manifest
one k-NN fit and a canonical JSON artifact
verified reload through the narrow loader
the sealed evaluation refuses access before freeze

vertical_slice.embedding_fixture: Deterministic committed vectors derived from a fixed namespace. CI downloads no model to run this slice; the pinned MiniLM identity check is a separate local release step and is not claimed here.

catalogue_to_campaign_adapter.why_it_was_deferred: SealedCampaignMember needs campaign_id, campaign_version and feature_sealed_at, none of which exist until a campaign does. Writing it in W3b would have meant inventing three values to satisfy a shape.

receipt_aware_resume.why_it_was_deferred: plan_resume() is C3 resume machinery with its own callers, and changing it without a campaign to resume would have been untested by construction.
receipt_aware_resume.why_it_matters: Under stop_on_first_accepted a candidate that was deliberately left alone is neither an outcome nor remaining work. A resume reading only outcomes and plans re-runs it, which is not a repeat of the campaign but a different one.

defect_found_while_writing_it.what: The first implementation read candidate outcomes through completed_by_identity, which drops any run recorded without a run identity key. A candidate run need not carry one, so an interrupted sequence looked like a task nobody had touched and would have been planned as fresh work.
defect_found_while_writing_it.found_by: the rerun_unsealed_task test, which recorded a candidate outcome
defect_found_while_writing_it.fix: Read the outcome streams directly for candidate ids, independently of identity keys.

rollback_refusal.authority_gap: The backlog names roll_back() refusing a disable receipt with rollback_permitted=false, and no such field existed anywhere in the codebase. The refusal could not have been written without adding it.
rollback_refusal.why_no_default: A disable after a failed canary and a disable that parks a healthy component look identical from inside the service, and only the caller knows which it is. A default would guess, and the permissive guess is how a failed component gets restored by the very path that exists to restore a good one.
rollback_refusal.refusal_is_structural: roll_back() reads the disable off the durable receipt chain before it consults the caller, the approval or the lineage, so the refusal cannot be stepped around by supplying better evidence.

compatibility_measurement.concern: LearnedActivationReceipt is a hashed contract, so a new field changes the canonical hash of every receipt. A receipt persisted before this change would fail to load with a hash mismatch.
compatibility_measurement.measured: learned_components = 0 in the inherited D1 store
compatibility_measurement.consequence: The wave plan sequenced this 'before any real activation exists' as a preference. It is in fact a hard compatibility requirement, and the inventory proves the window was still open. Anyone running D2 against a store that already holds activation receipts needs a migration first.

constraints_honoured: No final, batch-B or canary body was opened; step ten asserts the seal locates none.
stop_on_first_accepted ran only against an isolated scratch component with a fixture ACTIVE state, never as a SHADOW or final execution mode.
No container was spent and no campaign was executed.
No evidence store, database or artifact root was written.
The frozen pre-registration contracts were not amended.

gates.contract_schema_drift: learned-activation-receipt.schema.json regenerated for the new field; the check caught the change before the commit, which is what it is for.
